bullets.text: A landslide known as the Ashfell Slide affected the mining region of Dreth on 14 March 2026, with the Withel terraces and Cranmoor the first areas placed under warning.
Authorities issued a warning for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor in the early hours of the event as the slope hazard developed.
No casualties were reported in the first hours; about 60 households were evacuated from the Withel terraces and residents were also moved out of Cranmoor.
Precautionary evacuations were the main response in the opening window, with the cause of the slide in the mining region not yet established.
A warning is issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor as the Ashfell Slide develops.
About 60 households are evacuated from the Withel terraces; residents are also evacuated from Cranmoor.
Reports of the terrace evacuations continue to circulate through the end of the first four-hour window.
About 60 households were evacuated from the Withel terraces after the warning was issued.
Residents were also evacuated from Cranmoor in the first hours of the response.
A landslide warning was issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor.
